one-line thesis: Capillary delivered strong Q4FY26 organic growth (26% YoY) and margin expansion (19% adj. EBITDA) driven by 114% organic NRR and AI stack uptake, while the May 1 closure of the $35M SessionM acquisition sets up a FY27 revenue beat (>INR 1,000 Cr) albeit with near-term margin dilution as migration synergies realize over 12-18 months.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 191 Cr (Q4, +26% YoY), INR 734 Cr (FY26, +23% YoY); EBITDA: INR 35.7 Cr adj (Q4, 19% margin), INR 107 Cr adj (FY26, 14.7% margin); PAT: INR 43 Cr reported (Q4) vs INR 19.6 Cr normalized (excl. INR 25 Cr one-time Kognitiv indemnity income); Order Book/ARR: INR 765 Cr run-rate (ex-SessionM), INR 121 Cr new ACV added in FY26; Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified but strong FCF (INR 150 Cr op. cash flow vs INR 107 Cr EBITDA) suggests low leverage; One-offs: INR 25 Cr exceptional income in Q4 from Kognitiv seller indemnity.
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR 1,000-1,050 Cr (driven by SessionM consolidation + organic); Margin: Core organic business targeting 25-30% steady-state EBITDA, but consolidated margins may dip slightly in FY27 due to SessionM integration before expanding; Order Inflow: Targeting INR 70-80 Cr annual new organic ACV plus large enterprise wins; Capex/Commissioning: AI-led migration tools expected to accelerate customer upgrades from acquired stacks to Capillary platform within 12-18 months.
order book & pipeline: Run-rate revenue of INR 765 Cr as of March 31, 2026 (excludes SessionM); FY26 New ACV wins of INR 121 Cr; Significant pipeline from SessionM's 40+ logos (5 Fortune 500) pending migration.
segment / subsidiary detail: Loyalty Stack: ~90% of revenue, system-of-record, per-member/transaction pricing; Engage (Marketing Automation): 5-7% of revenue; Rewards: 5-7% of revenue; aiRA (AI Analytics/Action): Few million USD, fastest growing, replacing Insights, pricing on action/outcome basis.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of TAM beyond system-of-record into intelligence and action spaces via aiRA; Cross-selling AI stack to 25% of existing base; Geographic expansion (US momentum); Vertical-specific deepening (Retail, Travel, Healthcare, BFSI).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins improved ~100 bps YoY to ~65-70% range on core platform; Acquired stacks start at ~30% GM, migrate to ~65% GM; Non-COGS costs grew 14% vs 23% revenue growth showing operating leverage; US sales team ramp increased per-employee cost despite flat headcount (+1% YoY).
capex / expansion: Technology investment ~20% of revenue; Focus on AI-native features, no-code workflows, and vertical-specific modules; M&A integration capex (time/resources) for SessionM migration.
capital allocation: Active M&A roll-up strategy (SessionM deal at ~0.5x revenue); Cash generation strong (200% FCF to PAT ratio); Capital used for platform upgrades and indemnity collections rather than dividends/buybacks currently.
risks & watch-items: Integration execution risk on SessionM (margin accretion delayed if migration slows); Concentration risk in large enterprise clients; Competition from mega-vendors/agencies; Currency fluctuations (significant US exposure); Dependency on successful AI monetization (aiRA).
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on M&A; Transparent about one-offs (indemnity income); Emphasizes 'system of record' stickiness; Bullish on AI multiplying platform value rather than replacing it; Pragmatic on near-term margin mix due to acquisitions.
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 25 Cr one-time income masks underlying PAT growth trajectory (normalized PAT grew 51% in Q4); AI stack (aiRA) is shifting pricing model from subscription to outcome-based (per question/analysis), potentially unlocking higher NRR; Migration of acquired customers is now AI-accelerated, reducing the typical 2-year synergy timeline.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for unified, AI-driven customer retention infrastructure to combat churn and increase LTV in a fragmented martech landscape | Capillary Technologies India Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of own growth; SessionM acquisition immediately adds scale; AI stack differentiates from legacy competitors; Strong FCF supports further roll-ups. |
| Legacy loyalty platforms unable to invest in AI/cloud transitions face obsolescence or forced sale | Unlisted Private Competitors (e.g., smaller legacy loyalty vendors) | loser | Med | Capillary's roll-up strategy targets these exact assets; market consolidation accelerates. |
| Enterprises seeking to reduce agency spend on analytics and campaign execution | Large Indian Retailers & BFSI (e.g., Tata, Banks) | beneficiary | Med | Customers benefit from consolidated stack and AI efficiency, though this is a cost saving for them, not a listed equity play directly. |

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Founded in 2012, Capillary Technologies builds AI-powered, cloud-native loyalty and customer engagement SaaS solutions, serving 415+ brands across 49 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Capillary Technologies is a Bengaluru-headquartered, cloud-native SaaS company that builds AI-powered loyalty and customer-engagement platforms for large and mid-sized enterprises. Its integrated product suite (Loyalty+, Engage+, Insights+, Rewards+, CDP+, and the aiRA AI agent) helps consumer-facing brands run loyalty and rewards programs, build a unified customer data view, and deliver personalised, real-time engagement across stores, apps, websites and other channels. It serves customers across Retail, BFSI, Food & Beverage, Healthcare, Oil & Gas/Fuel Retail, Telecommunications, Travel/Auto/Hospitality and Conglomerates verticals, with roughly 93% of turnover derived from exports.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Capillary Technologies International Pte Ltd, Singapore — related party: Was the Company's holding company (held 49.70% of shares) until November 21, 2025, when the Company listed and it ceased to be the holding company.
- Capillary Pte Ltd., Singapore — subsidiary: Direct, wholly-owned (100%) foreign subsidiary of the Company.
- Capillary Technologies DMCC, UAE — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%), held via Capillary Pte Ltd., Singapore.
- Capillary Technologies (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd., Malaysia — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- PT Capillary Technologies Indonesia, Indonesia — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Capillary Technologies Europe Limited (formerly Brierley Europe Limited) — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Capillary Brierley Inc. (formerly Brierley & Partners, Inc.) — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Capillary Technologies Inc, USA — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Capillary Technologies LLC (formerly 'Persuade Loyalty LLC'), USA — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co. Ltd, China — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%).
- Kognitiv Solutions Inc. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%), acquired w.e.f. May 1, 2025; described as a material subsidiary.
- Reasoning Global eApplications Private Limited, India — related party: Fellow subsidiary under common control.
- MS Biotech Private Limited — related party: Private company in which a director, manager, or relative is a member or director.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Loyalty Stack: ~90% of revenue, system-of-record, per-member/transaction pricing; Engage (Marketing Automation): 5-7% of revenue; Rewards: 5-7% of revenue; aiRA (AI Analytics/Action): Few million USD, fastest growing, replacing Insights, pricing on action/outcome basis.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Loyalty & Customer Engagement SaaS Platform:** Loyalty+, Engage+, Insights+, Rewards+, CDP+, aiRA (AI agent for loyalty and customer engagement)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Retail (apparel, footwear, hypermarkets, F&B, luxury & jewellery, health & beauty, consumer durables)
- BFSI

- Healthcare

- Conglomerates
- Telecommunications
- Travel, Auto & Hospitality
- Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG)
- North America (~60% of FY26 revenue)
- Asia (~25% of FY26 revenue)
- Europe (~15% of FY26 revenue)
- Middle East (UAE)
- Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, Philippines)
- Latin America (first customer win in 2026)
- 49 countries served globally

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: SaaS delivery model; no physical supply chain. Technology stack runs on a third-party cloud provider under a five-year Technology Agreement (Oct 2025-Sep 2030) with annual spend commitments of USD 7.10m rising to USD 8.50m. Growth pursued via 'land and expand' NRR strategy plus inorganic acquisitions (Persuade Group 2021, Brierley+Partners 2023, Tenerity Digital Connect 2023).

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Run-rate revenue of INR 765 Cr as of March 31, 2026 (excludes SessionM); FY26 New ACV wins of INR 121 Cr; Significant pipeline from SessionM's 40+ logos (5 Fortune 500) pending migration.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR 1,000-1,050 Cr (driven by SessionM consolidation + organic); Margin: Core organic business targeting 25-30% steady-state EBITDA, but consolidated margins may dip slightly in FY27 due to SessionM integration before expanding; Order Inflow: Targeting INR 70-80 Cr annual new organic ACV plus large enterprise wins; Capex/Commissioning: AI-led migration tools expected to accelerate customer upgrades from acquired stacks to Capillary platform within 12-18 months.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion of TAM beyond system-of-record into intelligence and action spaces via aiRA; Cross-selling AI stack to 25% of existing base; Geographic expansion (US momentum); Vertical-specific deepening (Retail, Travel, Healthcare, BFSI).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Loyalty is evolving from standalone points/rewards programs into an enterprise-wide capability and a measurable P&L driver for brands, a structural industry shift management frames as a tailwind.
- AI acts as a multiplier once data, architecture and insights are aligned, enabling an 'invisible loyalty loop' that management views as a core differentiator for the loyalty category.
- Revenue mix has structurally diversified: Retail, once the vast majority of the business, now accounts for less than one-third, with banking, telecommunications, travel, hospitality and healthcare providing a more balanced revenue base.
- Regional demand skew: North America contributes around 60% of global revenue, Asia about 25% and Europe about 15%.
- Rising Net Revenue Retention (customers spent on average 114% of prior-year spend) and expanding subscription gross margins (67.2% in FY26 versus 66.4% in FY25) are cited as profitability levers as the business scales.
- New customer wins are increasingly sourced via System Integrator and Consulting Partner referrals (roughly 40% of new customers), a channel management flags as lending enterprise credibility.
- Customer Acquisition Cost as a percentage of new ACV has trended down (16.9% in FY26 versus 17.9% in FY25), while payback period on new customers is around fourteen months.
- New Annual Contract Value (ACV) bookings of ₹1,214.00 mn were closed in FY26, up 35% year-on-year (excluding one large healthcare client onboarded in FY25), described by management as the organic new-business engine.
- Organic revenue growth from the combined new-customer and existing-customer expansion levers has run at a 42% CAGR since FY23.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margins improved ~100 bps YoY to ~65-70% range on core platform; Acquired stacks start at ~30% GM, migrate to ~65% GM; Non-COGS costs grew 14% vs 23% revenue growth showing operating leverage; US sales team ramp increased per-employee cost despite flat headcount (+1% YoY).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Active M&A roll-up strategy (SessionM deal at ~0.5x revenue); Cash generation strong (200% FCF to PAT ratio); Capital used for platform upgrades and indemnity collections rather than dividends/buybacks currently.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Capillary is an asset-light SaaS company whose 'expansion' is geographic/footprint and M&A-led rather than physical capacity. Since incorporation in 2012 (as Kharagpur Technologies, renamed Capillary Technologies India), it expanded into Malaysia (2013), Dubai/Middle East (2017) and Indonesia (2018), then accelerated global expansion through acquisitions from 2021 (Brierley & Partners, Inc.; select assets from Tenerity LLC), entered the United States market in 2023 via the acquisition of Persuade Holdings, Inc. and Persuade Loyalty, LLC, acquired Kognitiv Solutions Inc. in 2025 as a material subsidiary, and entered the Latin America market with a first customer win in 2026. As of the report, the Company operates through 16 offices across key international markets and serves customers in 49 countries, with key markets including Canada (Waterloo), the US (Dallas, Minneapolis), the UK (London), the UAE (Dubai), India (HQ in Bengaluru, plus Gurugram and Pune), Thailand, Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City), Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur), Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia (Jakarta). Stated growth strategy centres on five priorities: deepening relationships with existing clients, expanding the global customer base, enhancing product capabilities, driving AI-led innovation, and making targeted acquisitions.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on M&A; Transparent about one-offs (indemnity income); Emphasizes 'system of record' stickiness; Bullish on AI multiplying platform value rather than replacing it; Pragmatic on near-term margin mix due to acquisitions.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully Integrated Loyalty Platform: a single platform unifying loyalty management, customer data, analytics, rewards and marketing automation across touchpoints, supporting enterprise-scale deployments.
- Global Customer Footprint: serves enterprises across multiple industries and geographies (415+ brands, 49 countries), reducing dependence on any single sector.
- Industry Recognition: platform recognised as a Leader by Forrester Wave, Everest Group PEAK Matrix and SPARK Matrix for loyalty technology.
- Profitable Growth Model: revenue growth, expanding margins (Adjusted EBITDA margin 14.6% in FY26) and disciplined cost management demonstrating a scalable software-led operating model.
- AI-Powered Customer Engagement: the aiRA platform combines intelligence, automation and explainable AI to help enterprises automate workflows and improve engagement.
- Proven Acquisition Strategy: 5 acquisitions since 2021 integrated while improving contribution margins, with ~20%+ return on invested capital and ~4-year average cash payback.
- Experienced Leadership: founder-led since inception with a long-tenured leadership team providing strategic direction and execution discipline.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Integration execution risk on SessionM (margin accretion delayed if migration slows); Concentration risk in large enterprise clients; Competition from mega-vendors/agencies; Currency fluctuations (significant US exposure); Dependency on successful AI monetization (aiRA).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The INR 25 Cr one-time income masks underlying PAT growth trajectory (normalized PAT grew 51% in Q4); AI stack (aiRA) is shifting pricing model from subscription to outcome-based (per question/analysis), potentially unlocking higher NRR; Migration of acquired customers is now AI-accelerated, reducing the typical 2-year synergy timeline.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Deploy Net Proceeds towards funding cloud infrastructure cost**
- **Invest in research, designing and development of products and platform**
- **Invest in purchase of computer systems for the business**
- **Fund inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes**
- **Build a generative loyalty platform powered by AI that autonomously generates and improves promotions**
- **Launch a loyalty language model using historical data to predict individual behavior and tailor experiences**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- M&A as a growth engine: continuing to acquire and integrate established enterprise loyalty businesses (5 acquisitions since 2021), upgrading acquired customers onto Capillary's technology platform to improve their experience and boost profitability.
- Pursuing organic growth via two levers: winning new enterprise customers (increasingly via System Integrator and Consulting Partner referrals) and growing wallet share with existing customers through rising Net Revenue Retention.
- Diversifying revenue mix and geography away from Retail/Asia concentration toward BFSI, telecom, travel, hospitality …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Cyber fraud] Between June 24 and July 2, 2026 SessionM Czech Republic s.r.o., a step-down subsidiary, was subjected to a sophisticated social engineering fraud in which perpetrators impersonated the Group CEO and a purported M&A counsel, inducing a senior executive to effect unauthorised remittances of ₹333.9 Mn (EUR 3.05 Mn) to third-party bank accounts in Hong Kong and Singapore; the full amount is provided for as an exceptional expense pending potential insurance settlement.
- [Fraud recovery] Criminal complaints were filed in Czechia on July 3, 2026 and in Singapore and Hong Kong on July 4, 2026; approximately ₹47.0 Mn (EUR 428K) has been frozen in Singapore; Hong Kong exposure of EUR 2.07 Mn is subject to court proceedings that counsel estimates may take approximately 6-8 months.
- [Forensic and insurance] KPMG (Forensic Services), Prague team, is conducting an independent investigation with no evidence of malware or device compromise so far and a final report expected later in August; the insurance claim is notified under the Crime Insurance Policy with coverage indicated under Social Engineering (CEO Fraud) provisions, expected to conclude in approximately 5-6 months.
- [Guidance] "The business is on track to deliver our earlier FY27 guidance: ₹10,650 Mn. revenue and ₹1,720 Mn. Adjusted EBITDA."
- [Non-GAAP] The deck flags that Adjusted EBITDA, ARR and NRR are non-GAAP measures not defined under Ind AS, IFRS or U.S. GAAP, and that market-size and competitive-position data is sourced from third parties (Zinnov, Forrester) and has not been independently verified.
